h: Postprandial RUQ pain, breath arrest on palpation (Murphy): referred pain site?
p: Acute cholecystitis irritates the diaphragm, referring pain to the right shoulder or scapula (phrenic nerve, C3-C5); ultrasound is the first test.

x: keyed diagnosis (SCLC) not unique from effusion/mass

h: Aplastic anemia (pancytopenia): which value is raised?
p: Marrow failure gives pancytopenia with low reticulocytes and compensatory high EPO; marrow is hypocellular, no splenomegaly. Treat with transplant or immunosuppression.

h: Erb palsy (C5-C6): which muscle is spared?
p: Upper trunk injury weakens deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus, biceps and brachialis (waiter's tip posture). Triceps (C6-C8, radial nerve) is spared.

h: Ethosuximide treats which seizure type?
p: Absence seizures: brief staring with eye fluttering, 3-Hz spike-and-wave on EEG, no postictal state; ethosuximide blocks T-type thalamic calcium channels.

h: Prolonged nitroprusside with rising lactate and shock: toxicity?
p: Nitroprusside releases cyanide; risk rises with high doses, prolonged use and renal failure. Treat with hydroxocobalamin or sodium nitrite plus thiosulfate.

h: Mandibular nerve (V3) exits the skull through which foramen?
p: V1 exits via the superior orbital fissure, V2 via foramen rotundum, V3 via foramen ovale; V3 also supplies the muscles of mastication.

h: Hyaline casts in an asymptomatic person: significance?
p: Hyaline (Tamm-Horsfall) casts appear in healthy people, especially after dehydration or exercise; RBC and WBC casts point to disease.

h: Acute inflammation edema: main mechanism?
p: Histamine and other mediators contract endothelial cells in venules, widening gaps and leaking protein-rich exudate.

h: Bricklayer with swollen, tender kneecap after kneeling: structure affected?
p: Prepatellar bursitis ('housemaid's knee') follows repetitive kneeling; anserine bursitis causes medial proximal tibial pain.

h: Itchy facial rash in a wheezy toddler: diagnosis?
p: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is part of the atopic triad with asthma and allergic rhinitis; infants have facial and extensor involvement.

h: Preterm neonate with abdominal distention: radiographic sign of NEC?
a: Gas within the bowel wall (pneumatosis intestinalis)
d: Positive group B strep blood cultures
p: Necrotizing enterocolitis occurs in premature infants after feeds, with pneumatosis intestinalis or portal venous gas; double bubble marks duodenal atresia.

h: Propranolol overdose with refractory bradycardia and hypotension: first-line antidote?
p: Glucagon raises cAMP independent of the blocked beta receptor, restoring inotropy and chronotropy; atropine is usually ineffective.

h: Lithium-induced diabetes insipidus: site of dysfunction?
p: Nephrogenic DI: high ADH with high serum sodium but the collecting duct cannot respond (loss of aquaporin-2 function); treat with amiloride and thiazides.

h: Drug inhibiting both thrombin and factor Xa via antithrombin?
p: UFH potentiates antithrombin, inhibiting IIa and Xa; LMWH and fondaparinux affect mainly Xa; apixaban directly inhibits Xa. UFH is preferred in unstable massive PE.

h: O mother, A baby, jaundice within 24 hours, weak direct Coombs: diagnosis?
p: ABO hemolytic disease occurs with type O mothers (anti-A/B IgG crossing the placenta) and is usually milder than Rh disease, with a weakly positive Coombs.

h: Which diabetes drug raises C-peptide levels?
p: Sulfonylureas close beta-cell K-ATP channels, increasing insulin and C-peptide release. Exogenous insulin suppresses C-peptide.

h: Tetracyclines (minocycline) in pregnancy: fetal toxicity?
a: Inhibited bone growth and tooth discoloration
p: Tetracyclines chelate calcium and deposit in bone and teeth: avoid in pregnancy and children under 8.

h: Rhyming speech ('pine, dine, doc'): thought process term?
p: Clang associations (words chosen by sound) are a disorganized thought form seen in schizophrenia and mania; flight of ideas keeps meaningful links.

h: Beta-blocker with intrinsic sympathomimetic activity?
p: Pindolol and acebutolol are partial agonists, causing less bradycardia; carvedilol is a mixed alpha/beta blocker and esmolol a short-acting beta-1 blocker.

h: Collagen type of reticular fibers and early granulation tissue?
p: Type III (reticulin) dominates early wound healing and is later replaced by type I; type II is cartilage and type IV is basement membrane.

h: Early diabetic nephropathy with microalbuminuria: biopsy finding?
p: Microalbuminuria (30-300 mg/day) accompanies GBM thickening and mesangial expansion; nodular glomerulosclerosis comes later with overt proteinuria. ACE inhibitors slow progression.

h: Candida infection that is AIDS-defining?
p: Candida esophagitis (odynophagia, white plaques) indicates advanced immunosuppression, unlike oral or vaginal candidiasis which occur in healthy hosts.

h: Oocyte arrest points in meiosis (primary, secondary)?
p: Primary oocytes arrest in prophase I until puberty (resume at ovulation); secondary oocytes arrest in metaphase II until fertilization.
